audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names Aurora's abilities wrongly throughout. It invents 'Vile Flowers' as her passive (whys[3], spikes[0], early, wants.foe[0]) — her passive is Spirit Abjuration. It calls Between Worlds her E and describes it as a 'dash into stun combo' (whys[3], spikes[0], early, wants.foe[1]) — Between Worlds is her R. And it calls The Weirding her R (spikes[1], mid, wants.foe[2]) — The Weirding is her E. The two are swapped and a fourth ability is fabricated.
audit.why: Kit file is authoritative: P Spirit Abjuration, Q Twofold Hex, W Across the Veil, E The Weirding, R Between Worlds. A reader tracking 'Vile Flowers' stacks is tracking nothing.
audit.corrected: Vile Flowers -> Spirit Abjuration / spirits; Between Worlds restored to (R); The Weirding restored to (E) with its real behaviour — blast, slow, then hop backward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Abjuration heals Aurora off spirits exorcised from enemies she damages, and nothing on the page said so — the anti-heal timing question was never raised.
audit.why: It is the missingInteractions entry for this matchup and it decides every extended trade: chip damage pays her back.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, enemyWin, breakdown.early, breakdown.feeding, report[5], dontsFull[2], whys[3], early and wants.foe[0].

notes:
BIGGEST FINDING: the content layer had Aurora's E and R swapped and invented a fourth ability. 'Vile Flowers' (whys[3], spikes[0], early, wants.foe[0]) does not exist — her passive is Spirit Abjuration. Between Worlds was labelled (E) and described as a dash-into-stun (whys[3], spikes[0], early, wants.foe[1]) — it is her R. The Weirding was labelled (R) (spikes[1], mid, wants.foe[2]) — it is her E, a blast-and-slow that hops her BACKWARD, which is nearly the opposite of an engage. All corrected against the kit file.

RATING: 55.02% over 927 games graded TRICKY at 7/10. Moved to EVEN / 5.5/10 with the tone colour and both rating lines. carryRating left at 7.5/10.

CHART: full-layer sides read Aurora/Aurora/Skill x5 against content win[] and packet.levelChart, which both read Skill/Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko — all seven rows disagreed. Moved the full layer onto the content layer; no win[N] edits possible (before would equal after). content mid and whys[4] were both arguing level 6 belongs to Aurora, directly under a row saying Ekko — corrected.

ADDED: Spirit Abjuration heals her off spirits exorcised from enemies she damages (the missingInteractions entry) — this is the Grievous Wounds decision the page never mentioned. Also the 140s-vs-110s ultimate asymmetry, which is why level 6 turns.

FLAG CONFLICT, handled per the brief's rule: Aurora's R carries a 'hardCC' derived flag, but Riot's own text for Between Worlds says it 'damages and slows' with no stun. I wrote slow everywhere and never claimed a stun. Worth a data-side check on that flag.

SUSPECT NAME: packet flagged wants.foe[1] 'Use Between Worlds' — the name is real but was attached to the wrong ability's behaviour; my edit removes it from that slot entirely.

REPORT SWEEP: one substantive rewrite (report[5]); report[0]/[1]/[3]/[4] are lint-mandated pronoun corrections carried in step with their source fields; report[14] follows the rating change.

LEFT ALONE (templated, nothing groundable without inventing): report[9], report[10], report[11], report[12], content late, spikes[2]/[3], whys[0]/[1]/[5]/[6], wants.you[*].

UNVERIFIED, not written: whether Across the Veil's invisibility can be broken by Ekko's W anomaly or revealed by his passive; whether Twofold Hex's recast can be dodged once the curse is applied; Between Worlds' teleport rules for enemies. None claimed.
